headline: Postpaid growth holds but integration costs pressure margins
summary_short: T-Mobile's revenue rose 7.8% y/y to $22.79B in the quarter ended June 30, 2026, with diluted EPS up 5.3% to $2.99, while net income was roughly flat at $3.24B as UScellular integration costs and higher depreciation and interest expense offset postpaid growth.
summary_long: Postpaid revenue rose 13% y/y on higher account growth (including the UScellular and Metronet acquisitions) and postpaid ARPA up 2% to $152.91. Total revenue grew 7.8% to $22.79B. Operating expenses rose 9% on integration, severance, and D&A tied to UScellular, holding operating margin roughly flat at 24.1% (-0.6ppt y/y) and net margin to 14.2% (-1.0ppt) as net income grew just 0.5% to $3.24B despite the top-line gain. The company paid $1.1B in dividends ($1.02/share) and repurchased $2.2B of stock in the quarter under its $18.2B 2026 Stockholder Return Program (raised from $14.6B in April). Cash fell to $2.8B from $10.3B a year ago on debt paydown and buybacks. No explicit forward guidance figures were restated in this filing.

drivers.explanation: Postpaid revenue growth was driven by higher average postpaid accounts, including the UScellular and Metronet acquisitions, and higher postpaid ARPA.
Total operating expenses rose 9% y/y on higher D&A, SG&A, and interest expense tied to UScellular integration, offsetting revenue growth.
Growth was muted by $146M of UScellular merger-related costs including accelerated depreciation (vs $25M a year ago) and higher interest expense on higher average debt.
Board raised the 2026 Stockholder Return Program authorization to $18.2B from $14.6B while UScellular integration continued to weigh on near-term margins even as postpaid growth accelerated.
